description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
In project year 1 ample progress was made in reaching the project level outputs: A blended master teacher course was rolled out, in which participants from all 3 Ethiopian universities participated. In this Master teacher course, the participants were introduced to interactive 21st century didactics, to the topic of teaching IDP/refugee students (especially related to dealing with trauma) and to health education through the child-to-child approach. So far, two face-to-face training activities have been conducted and many online sessions were held. A start was made with the next step: the development of a teacher training courses for the primary school teachers in IDP and refugee camps. This course will include teaching skills, dealing with trauma of the students and health education. Each university will develop their own course, tailored to the local circumstances in the IDP and refugee camps. The development of these courses, and the implementation (training of primary school teachers) will further continue in project year 2.
The development of three research proposals has also started, each proposal related to education and IDP/refugees.
The research topics are:
• Addis: Evaluating Ethiopian Government’s commitment to provide education to urban refugees in Addis Ababa. Subquestion: Assess the challenges refugees, host communities and institutions (both governmental and non-governmental) face in providing education to urban refugees in Addis Ababa.
• Gambella: Status, needs, challenges and opportunities of primary education in refugee setting: the case of refugee camps in Gambella
• Jigjiga: Children education in displacement: exploring the educational experience of displaced children in Woloji IDP camp in Somali regional sate of Ethiopia
The universities are supported in conducting research via online training activities. These online activities guide the participants step by step through the conduction of research, starting with defining the research question, selecting methodology and eventually the data analysis and write up. The conclusions of the research feed into the knowledge body of the universities as expert centers on refugees and education. In the case of Gambella and Jigjiga, the research will also strengthen the relationship between the universities and the nearby refugee camps.
For both the Master teacher training and the research course, at least 33% female participants was ensured.
Lastly, in year 1 a start was made for collaboration of the three Ethiopian universities with other relevant institutes in the region. The kick off was an important event for this, with senior staff from UNESCO, Ethiopian Education and Research Network (EthERNet) and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) present. During this meeting, the project plans were shared and possibilities for future collaboration were discussed. Over the course of project year one, frequent moments of informal contact took place. For year two another online event is planned, which will take place after the implementation of the teacher trainers course in refugee camps.
